classes_covered: secrets shipped in public JS bundles (L1 since v1.3)
directory listing / risky HTTP methods / exposed API docs (L2)
Supabase live anon RLS probe (L3 v0.4 — read-only GET)
restricted differential access check (L3 v1.0 — --active-tests, GET-only, verified ownership, owner identities)
classes_not_covered: authenticated-area testing & business-logic flaws beyond the restricted differential check
injection testing (XSS/SQLi canaries — delegated: init-zap generates the ZAP baseline config, v1.0 decision)
full DAST / fuzzing (by design — delegated to the generated ZAP config)
server internals, databases, queues (black-box view only — pair with Codebase Mode)

score_breakdown.note: Low-confidence findings and INFO do not deduct. Repeats of the same root cause add +10% each, capped at 2× the severity weight (v1.3).

findings.title: Secret shipped in a public JavaScript bundle (supabase)

evidence.note: JWT-shaped token — confirmed below by decoding the role claim

findings.fix: Remove the secret from any code reachable by the client build, move it to server-side env only, rotate the credential at the provider (rotate-first), then purge old bundles/CDN cache.

remediation.steps: Rotate the credential at the provider dashboard FIRST, then remove it from client code, then purge CDN/edge cache of old bundles.

findings.title: Secret shipped in a public JavaScript bundle (stripe)
findings.fix: Remove the secret from any code reachable by the client build, move it to server-side env only, rotate the credential at the provider (rotate-first), then purge old bundles/CDN cache.

remediation.steps: Rotate the credential at the provider dashboard FIRST, then remove it from client code, then purge CDN/edge cache of old bundles.

findings.title: Sensitive file publicly served: /.env

evidence.note: env file with secret-shaped values is publicly served

findings.fix: Remove /.env from the web root / deny serving it at the edge, rotate anything it contains (rotate-first), and purge CDN cache. Code map: the deployment pipeline is shipping dotfiles — check Dockerfile COPY scope, .dockerignore, static host config (e.g. `vercel.json`, `netlify.toml`), and the web root contents.

remediation.steps: Treat every value in the exposed env file as compromised: rotate at the provider FIRST, then remove the file from the web root, then purge CDN/edge cache.

findings.title: Sensitive file publicly served: /db.sql

evidence.note: SQL dump (CREATE/INSERT statements) is publicly downloadable

findings.fix: Remove /db.sql from the web root / deny serving it at the edge, rotate anything it contains (rotate-first), and purge CDN cache. Code map: run Codebase Mode (anubis-guardian scan .) on the repository to map this to exact file:line.

findings.title: Site served over plain HTTP (no TLS)

evidence.note: every request — including session cookies — travels in cleartext

findings.fix: Serve over HTTPS (terminate TLS at the edge/provider, redirect http→https, enable HSTS once stable).

findings.title: Session cookie "sid" set without HttpOnly (readable by any XSS)
findings.fix: Set HttpOnly on "sid" — session cookies must never be readable from JS.

findings.title: TRACE method enabled (reflects requests — XST)

evidence.masked: TRACE returned 200 and reflected the request

findings.fix: Disable TRACE at the server/edge (nginx: trace_method off; most platforms deny it by default).

findings.title: Exposed source map ships original sources with secret-shaped content
findings.fix: Disable source maps in production builds; remove .map files from the deployed bundle and purge the CDN cache. Code map: next.config.js `productionBrowserSourceMaps` or the bundler config that emits .map files into the public build.

findings.title: Exposed file: /.git/config
findings.fix: Remove /.git/config from the web root / deny serving it at the edge, rotate anything it contains (rotate-first), and purge CDN cache. Code map: the web server is serving the repository folder — check nginx root config / static host rules; the .git dir must never be inside the web root.

findings.title: Cookie "sid" set without the Secure flag

evidence.note: cookie can travel over plain http

findings.fix: Set the Secure attribute on "sid" (and serve the site over https only).

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy header missing
findings.fix: Serve a Content-Security-Policy header (start with a report-then-enforce rollout; script-src 'self', no unsafe-inline for new code). Code map: middleware.ts (response headers) or next.config.js headers()/async headers — or the reverse proxy (nginx/vercel.json).

findings.title: Clickjacking protection missing (no X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
findings.fix: Serve X-Frame-Options: DENY (or CSP frame-ancestors 'none') so the site cannot be framed by attacker pages. Code map: middleware.ts (response headers) or next.config.js headers()/async headers — or the reverse proxy (nginx/vercel.json).

findings.title: Permissive Allow header advertises risky methods (PUT, DELETE)
findings.fix: Restrict allowed methods to what the app uses (GET/POST/HEAD); disable WebDAV-style verbs at the edge.

findings.title: Directory listing enabled: /backup/
findings.fix: Disable autoindex for /backup/ at the server/edge (nginx autoindex off; S3/CDN bucket policy) — listing exposes files no page links to. Code map: the deployment pipeline is shipping dotfiles — check Dockerfile COPY scope, .dockerignore, static host config (e.g. `vercel.json`, `netlify.toml`), and the web root contents.

findings.title: Swagger UI exposed on production
findings.fix: Disable Swagger UI outside development (NestJS SwaggerModule setup gated by NODE_ENV; GraphQL introspection off in prod), or protect it behind auth. Code map: run Codebase Mode (anubis-guardian scan .) on the repository to map this to exact file:line.

findings.title: Cookie "sid" set without SameSite
findings.fix: Set SameSite=Lax (or Strict) on "sid" to blunt CSRF.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options header missing
findings.fix: Serve X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all responses. Code map: middleware.ts (response headers) or next.config.js headers()/async headers — or the reverse proxy (nginx/vercel.json).

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.fix: Serve Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or stricter). Code map: middleware.ts (response headers) or next.config.js headers()/async headers — or the reverse proxy (nginx/vercel.json).

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
findings.fix: Serve a Permissions-Policy restricting camera/microphone/geolocation to none (or first-party only). Code map: middleware.ts (response headers) or next.config.js headers()/async headers — or the reverse proxy (nginx/vercel.json).

findings.title: Server header discloses a specific version
findings.fix: Strip or genericize the Server header version at the edge (banner disclosure feeds attacker recon).

findings.title: X-Powered-By header discloses the stack
findings.fix: Remove X-Powered-By at the server/proxy (e.g. helmet.hidePoweredBy / proxy hideHeaders).

findings.title: security.txt absent (RFC 9116)
findings.fix: Publish /.well-known/security.txt so researchers can report issues safely.

findings.title: Public bundle references internal/localhost endpoints
findings.fix: Remove internal hostnames from client code; route internal calls through a server-side proxy.

findings.title: Technology fingerprint: express, nextjs
findings.fix: Informational — findings below pair with code-map hints per detected framework.

findings.title: Bundle references a sourceMappingURL (check exposure at Level 2)
findings.fix: A .map file is referenced next to http://127.0.0.1:57583/_next/static/app.js. Level 2 checks whether it is actually exposed and ships original sources.

authorization.note: self-attested (local only) — not proof; report consumers should treat Level 2+ results accordingly
